findings.element: horizon() (render-b.js:90-99, the .b-num / .b-unit pair at 92-95) and card() (render-b.js:1046-1055, .b-ogNum / .b-ogDate at 1050-1051), against F.fmt.dayCount in fixture.js and the assertion at interaction-check.mjs:370
findings.problem: Driven, not read. Set F.project.primaryDate.date one day out and remount: the horizon reads "1 DAYS" on phone, on desk and on owner-flight — that is the 96px figure on a phone and the 148px figure at desk, the largest object in the design. Set it to today and it reads "0 DAYS"; set it six days back and it reads "-6 DAYS". The unfurl card is the same shape: driving F.toDay() to 1, 0 and -5 printed "1 · days to Saturday 3 October 2026", "0 · days to …" and "-5 · days to …", with the aria-label unchanged throughout. The fix already exists in the file the numbers come from: fixture.js carries fmt.dayCount under the comment "'1 days' is the kind of thing that makes a person stop trusting a screen. The plural lives here, once", and the horizon and the card are the only two counting surfaces in the lab that never call it — the editor readout (render-b.js:460, 652) and the row's accessible name (105) both do. The arrival was solved once, by hand, as a separate frame: states.day writes the word "Today" as a literal at 1126, and that frame is reachable only by ?state=day, so every artifact a guest actually opens counts down through zero and out the other side. The assertion written to guard exactly this cannot see it. interaction-check.mjs:370 is /\b1 days\b/ against innerText; .b-unit is uppercased in CSS so the string on the page is "1 DAYS", and the test runs on owner-editing after a stepper press, where the horizon is counting to the wedding and not to the row that moved. It is the round-3 class again — an assertion passing by proving the wrong property — sitting on the biggest number in the product.
findings.fix: Put the whole rendering of the count in the one place that owns plurals. In fixture.js beside fmt.dayCount add: fmt.countdown = function (n) { if (n > 1) return { num: String(n), unit: "days" }; if (n === 1) return { num: "1", unit: "day" }; if (n === 0) return { word: "Today" }; return { word: "That day has gone" }; }. In horizon() replace lines 92-95 with var c = F.fmt.countdown(daysFrom(clock, F.project.primaryDate.date)); and emit c.word ? h("p.b-dayCount", { text: c.word }) : h("div.b-count", {}, [h("span.b-num.num", { text: c.num }), h("span.b-unit", { text: c.unit })]) — .b-dayCount already exists at b.css:903 at the display step the morning was designed on, so the arrival re-uses the register instead of inventing a second one. In card() do the same at 1050-1051: c.word ? one line in the sans face at the card's own display step : h("p.b-ogNum.num", { text: c.num }) plus "day to "/"days to " + F.fmt.longYear(date). Then replace interaction-check.mjs:370 with a loop: for each of phone, desk, print, owner-flight, publish and unfurl, set F.project.primaryDate.date = F.plusDays(F.today, k) for k of [2, 1, 0, -3], remount, and assert that at k=1 the body text matches /\b1 day\b/i and not /\b1 days\b/i, at k=0 it contains "Today" and matches neither /\b0 days?\b/i nor /-\d/, and at k=-3 no negative numeral appears anywhere on the page.

findings.element: states.day (render-b.js:1119-1138), the single todayItems[0] at 1133, against ahead() (56-62) and behind() (66-70)
findings.problem: Driven with the product's own controls at 390 and at 1440. From owner-editing I typed "3 October 2026" into the editor's date field — the wedding day is the ceiling the editor accepts, not past it — and the reversibility bar confirmed "Send the invitations moved 56 days later." The record now holds two live moments on 2026-10-03. Switch to the morning and it reads, in 24px semibold under the rule: "HAPPENING NOW / Send the invitations at The Orchard". The wedding is not on the wedding morning. todayItems is filtered correctly at 1121 and then only [0] is rendered, in fixture array order, which is neither chronological nor chosen; every other moment on the day is erased from the whole screen, because ahead() takes days > 0 and behind() takes days < 0 and nothing dated on the clock has anywhere else to go. The count under it contradicts it in the same frame: "HOW YOU GOT HERE 8 MOMENTS" while the plan holds 9. Repeated by pushing a ceremony and a dinner onto the day: neither string appears anywhere in document.body.innerText and the behind count stays at 9 while the record holds 11. This is the flagship screen and the ordinary case, not an edge — a wedding morning has a ceremony, a photograph, a dinner and a first dance on it, and the editor invites the owner to place every one of them there. All 424 assertions pass on it, because the day block is graded once against an untouched fixture that happens to hold exactly one moment on the day, and the two assertions that prove a shared day ("they are grouped, not overprinted", "the day says how many it holds") test the measure, which the morning never renders.
findings.fix: Render the day rather than the first row of it. Replace render-b.js:1131-1134 with h("section.b-dayNow", {}, [h("h2.b-behindLabel", { text: todayItems.length > 1 ? "Today" : F.stateLabel.now }), h("ul.b-dayList", { role: "list", "aria-label": "What is happening today" }, todayItems.map(function (m, i) { return h("li.b-dayItem", { role: "listitem" }, [h(i === 0 ? "p.b-dayNowTitle" : "p.b-dayAlso", { text: nameOf(m) })]); }))]) with .b-dayAlso set at 20px/600 on the existing --lead-head and --track-head so the day keeps a lead without a second register. Head it "Today" above two or more, because "Happening now" over four moments is false of three of them. Then assert it: push two moments dated F.project.primaryDate.date into F.milestones, remount ?state=day, and require every one of their titles to appear in document.body.innerText, the behind count to equal F.milestones.filter(function (m) { return !m.date || F.days(clock, m.date) < 0; }).length, and the moments listed on the day plus the moments listed behind to sum to F.milestones.length — the property that would have caught this and that nothing in the suite currently holds.

findings.element: render-b.js:95 (.b-sub in the horizon) and render-b.js:1133 (.b-dayNowTitle), against fixture.js PROJECT, and the assertion at interaction-check.mjs:712
findings.problem: " at The Orchard" is a string literal in the renderer, typed in two places, and it is the only fact on the entire artifact that tells a guest where to go. It prints on every surface that carries the horizon — phone, desk, print, owner-flight, owner-editing, publish — and again on the wedding morning. Nothing in the record holds it: fixture.js's PROJECT has slug, name, oneLiner and primaryDate {label, date} and no place at all, and workspace.name is "The Orchard, events", which is the planner's business rather than the couple's venue. The name collision is what makes the literal look derived when it is not. The fixture's own header states the contract this breaks — "Nothing here is placeholder text… if a number appears on a surface it is derived from this object through one accessor" — and the defect library names the class outright ("Fixture names leak. Content is a named person or it is a bug"). Concatenating a place onto a moment's title is also what produced "Send the invitations at The Orchard" in the finding above: the sentence is synthesised, so it will weld the venue to whatever string happens to sort first. The gate proves it by matching the typed string: interaction-check.mjs:712 is ok("the day names where to be", /Wedding day at The Orchard/.test(text)), which is true of the literal and would stay true if the couple were being married somewhere else entirely.
findings.fix: Put it on the record and read it once. fixture.js: primaryDate: { label: "Wedding day", date: "2026-10-03", place: "The Orchard, Adare" }. render-b.js:95 becomes h("p.b-sub", { text: F.project.primaryDate.label + (F.project.primaryDate.place ? " at " + F.project.primaryDate.place : "") }). render-b.js:1133 stops concatenating entirely — the title is the title — and the place becomes its own line inside .b-dayNow, h("p.b-dayWhere", { text: "At " + F.project.primaryDate.place }) at 15px on --fore-62, stated once for the day rather than glued to each moment, and omitted when place is absent. Then change interaction-check.mjs:712 to read the record instead of the string: set F.project.primaryDate.place = "Ballyvaughan House", remount ?state=day and ?state=phone, and require document.body.innerText to contain "Ballyvaughan House" and not to contain "The Orchard" outside a milestone title.

findings.problem: aria-label on a link replaces its whole subtree in the accessibility tree. Driven at 390 and at 1440: the card's rendered text is "MARA & FINN / 79 / days to Saturday 3 October 2026 / Mara & Finn, a wedding timeline / timeline.signalstudio.ie" and its accessible name is exactly "Mara & Finn, a wedding timeline" — nothing more. The count is the reason the card exists; it is set at 64px in the mono face with tabular figures, its own display tracking and --lead-display, and it is announced to nobody. So is the date. This is the first Signal surface a guest ever meets, it is the only focusable element on the state, and for anyone using a screen reader it carries one sentence that is already printed underneath it in .b-unfurlTitle. The floor assertion that covers this ground — "every visible interactive element has an accessible name" — passes: there is a name, it just is not the card. No other control in the lab does this; every other label is built from what the control shows.
findings.fix: Delete the aria-label from render-b.js:1046 — h("a.b-unfurl", { href: F.shareUrlFull }, [...]) — and let the card name itself from its subtree, which already reads "Mara & Finn, 79, days to Saturday 3 October 2026, Mara & Finn, a wedding timeline, timeline.signalstudio.ie". Then assert the property rather than the presence: open ?state=unfurl, require document.querySelector(".b-unfurl").getAttribute("aria-label") === null, and take page.accessibility.snapshot() and require the link node's name to contain both F.project.name and String(F.toDay()). Add the same shape to the floor check at interaction-check.mjs:82-88: an element whose aria-label omits a number that is visible inside it is a name that lost content, and should fail there for every state, not just this card.

findings.element: states.loading (render-b.js:1180-1199) and its comment at 1188-1191, against field() (render-b.js:308-312) and the real horizon measured at 390
findings.problem: Two measurements, both at 390. (a) The frame paints a grey bar over a fact it demonstrably already has. field() labels the region "The plan for Mara & Finn", so in the same frame the loading state tells a screen reader the couple's name and shows the eye a 17px rectangle where that name goes. The project name is not pending — it is in the link before anything is fetched — and this is the one guest state in the lab with no h1 at all. (b) The reserve is 19px wrong and the comment states a third number again: line 1188-1191 says the horizon "is 271px". Measured, the real horizon at phone medium runs from 26 to 301 in the field, height 275; the loading stack runs from 26 to 320. Bar for bar against the real object — who 17 / count 86 / when 26 / sub 23, margins 22, 10, 4, then the rule at +26, the label at +8 and the note at +14 — the skeleton's count bar is 83 rather than 86 and its margins are 22, 14, 10 with 26 before the closing sentence. So the page lifts 19px when the plan lands, under a comment claiming it was measured. Nothing in the gate reads this geometry; "the loading frame invents no measure" and "nothing shimmers" both pass.
findings.fix: (a) Replace the first skeleton at render-b.js:1192 with the real heading: h("h1.b-who", { text: F.project.name, style: "margin-bottom:22px" }). It occupies the identical 17px slot, it gives the state the h1 every other guest surface has, and it stops the frame hiding something it holds. (b) Three numbers: 1193 height 83 → 86 and margin-bottom 14 → 10; 1194 margin-bottom 10 → 4; 1198 margin-top 26 → 14. The stack then ends at 301, exactly where the horizon ends, and the page does not move on arrival. Correct the 271 in the comment to 275 or delete the number. Then assert it instead of commenting it: open ?state=loading and ?state=phone at 390, take the bottom of the last node before the measure in each, measured from .b-field's top, and require the two to agree within 1px.

biggestWin: Score 7.8, up from 7.6, and the rise is earned by the owner's side rather than talked into existence. Everything round 3 confirmed is genuinely fixed and I re-drove each one: the reversibility bar now sits inside the panel at 1280 and 1440 and never touches the count, hiding a moment removes it from the guest list, the record room and the printed keepsake list the past in full with no dead control, the DOM order matches the painted order after twenty presses, and the way back out of Preview is visible. 424 assertions, no console errors, no sideways scroll at any of the four widths, and the whole thing is written against declared ladders rather than hand-tuned values — the craft plumbing under this is better than most shipped products have. What stands between it and 9.5 is not that work. It is the guest side, which had never been graded, and specifically the two objects that carry the number this product is about. The horizon reads "1 DAYS" the day before the wedding, "0 DAYS" on the morning and "-6 DAYS" after it, on every surface a guest opens, and the unfurl card that lands in the message does the same — while the fixture already contains the accessor written to prevent exactly that and neither of them calls it. The arrival was solved once, beautifully, as a hand-authored frame at ?state=day that no guest can reach. And that frame itself names the wrong thing: put a second moment on the wedding day, which the editor explicitly lets the owner do, and the wedding morning reads "Happening now — Send the invitations at The Orchard" with the wedding gone and the count beneath it off by one. The venue in that sentence is a string typed into the renderer twice and derived from nothing. For the founder: what remains is one build and one decision, not polish. The build is half a day — make the countdown one accessor with an arrival branch, make the morning render the day as a list instead of its first row, and put the venue on the record. The decision is smaller but worth taking deliberately: the morning is currently 259 characters and gives a guest standing outside a venue nothing they can act on, because the product has no notion of a time or a place, only of a day. That is the only place where I would spend more than a day, and it is the screen everything else gets judged by. Three of my five findings passed both gates; two of them passed an assertion written specifically to guard the ground they broke, which is now the third round running that the gates have proved the wrong property. Fix the five, and change the plural and arrival assertions to read the fixture rather than the rendered string, and I would put this at 9.3.
